sentence: This project builds an approach that combines imaging in living animals with immune cell profiling to find out how pancreatic cancer avoids the immune system.
This project trains graduate researchers to use engineering methods to tackle problems in cancer biology, diagnosis, and treatment.
This project builds a way to label Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cells with nanobubbles so their movement can be watched using ultrasound.
This project provides sequencing tools and computer methods that let cancer researchers study genes in single cells and in tissue.
This project studies how Nras mutations, PDL1, and UVB light work together in melanomas and how they affect tumor spread and treatment resistance.
This project provides a facility that makes very small devices, including lab-on-a-chip devices, for studying cells and disease.
This project builds computer methods that find genetic variants, including mosaic mutations, from long sequence reads.
This project builds chemical probes and imaging tools that show reactive oxygen and nitrogen molecules inside living cells.
This project studies heart disease in people living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa and tries to find better ways to screen for it.
This project provides tools to switch genes on or off across whole sets of genes, using RNA interference and CRISPR, to study cancer.
This project tests short guide molecules that direct the cell's own enzymes to repair mutations in mRNA, so cells can make working protein.
This project trains researchers in medical genetics.
This project uses genetics and proteomics to build models that predict dementia risk from blood plasma and DNA.
This project builds machine learning and statistical tools that find biological patterns inside single cells from spatial transcriptomics data.
This project tests whether losing PD-1 signaling makes CD4 T cells react to the body's own tissue and causes side effects in cancer patients.
This project builds materials that help the body heal, to repair damaged muscle and bone together after serious limb injuries.
This project uses viruses guided by nanobodies or peptides to deliver molecules that disable HIV DNA hiding in infected human cells.
This project uses imaging and mouse genetics to find how blood vessel surroundings in bone marrow control the making of blood cells.
This project builds a way to sense small molecules using E. coli, so enzymes that make small molecules can be evolved.
This project builds a controller for a robotic exoskeleton that helps people keep their balance while standing and walking.
